proof:
At the old center, the energy is two by Jensen applied to every admissible denominator and equality at the constant denominator. For either unit continuous orientation and any base tilt, the own contribution is $1+\delta$. The two endpoint contributions sum to at least two: before adding $\delta$ their two thresholds are opposite, so reflection pairs the captured lengths to two, and adding a nonnegative margin to both cannot reduce them. Steep finite tilts attain two by making one endpoint interval full and the other empty. At the source the two closed pure-base caps have mass four. Thus the actual raw depth at the center is $Q$. Endpoint bases have pure-base caps of mass two. At middle mark $(0,y)$ the shift is $\delta(y)=\delta\sqrt{1-y^2}$ by the interval formula of 8cc17f76507d258f, including the zero boundary value. The two normals $(4,\pm1)$ have saturated endpoint traces for all $|y|\le1$. Depth at least $Q$ therefore forces $y-\delta(y)\le-\delta$ and $-y-\delta(y)\le-\delta$: otherwise the corresponding own cut captures strictly less than $1+\delta$. Their sum forces $y=0$. This proves global uniqueness. The stated selected caps both have mass $Q$; the first has an outside-supporting point at base $-1$ and a strict-full endpoint fiber at $1$, while the second has strictly empty/full endpoint fibers. Their weighted continuous normal is zero and the old exact assigned margin on the middle interval is $\delta-\delta(y)\ge0$.

The radius interpolation is affine in $z$, so both signs of $h$ give actual compatible positive fibers for small $t$. Their mass is $M_t=6-3ht$. At the centered mark $E_t(0)=2-ht$ by Jensen, and $E_t(0)/M_t=1/3$. Their variance is $\Sigma_t=(r_-^3+r_0^3+r_+^3)/(3(r_-+r_0+r_+))$, whose derivative at zero is $-h/3$. Consequently the centered shift $\delta_t=\varepsilon\sqrt{\Sigma_t/3}$ has derivative $-\delta h/2$. At any mark the constant denominator gives energy at most the own interval length, with the maximum at the centered mark. Since the weighted continuous normal is zero, the exact current assigned minimum is $\alpha(t)=\delta-\delta_t$. The two cap tails at threshold increases $tr$ have first losses
$$
R_+(r)=h/2+r-(-r-h)_+,\qquad R_-(r)=h/2+r .
$$
These follow by direct interval clipping: the middle cut is proper, the right endpoint is still full with no radius change, and the first cap alone can acquire a segment $t(-r-h)_+$ at base $-1$. The exact inverse proof of 9ee0d9a1e9f65259 applies to these actual tails at fixed normals: the local tails are strictly decreasing through the proper own cut and the true budget has derivative $\delta h/2$. Thus the continued first loss solves $R_+(r_+)=R_-(r_-)=\ell$ and $r_++r_-=\delta h$. If $h\ge0$, the two threshold shifts are both $\delta h/2$ and the outside hinge vanishes. If $h\le0$, solving the active affine branch gives $r_+=(\delta-1)h/3\le-h$ and the stated second slope. The inequalities verify the actual branch selection. Subtracting $(3+\delta)h/2=(Q/M)3h$ gives the normalized improvement and the two slopes give the stated Jensen gap. The exact current weighted margins cover the assigned middle interval, and endpoint pure-base caps stay strictly cheaper for small $t$. Thus this is the response of an actual continued cover; it need not equal the new globally optimized depth.
statement:
In $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R$, take the three interval fibers $K_z=[-1,1]$ at $z=-1,0,1$ of the rectangle $[-1,1]^2$. Use summed interval length $M=6$, projective energy $E_K(y)=\inf_a\int_K[1+a(X-y)]^{-2}\,dX$ over positive denominators, pooled within-fiber variance $\Sigma=1/3$, and the invariant buffered margin
$$
a(z-p)+u(X-y)+\varepsilon (E_{K_p}(y)/M)^{1/2}|u|\sqrt{\Sigma}.
$$
Pure-base caps are closed and unbuffered. Let $0<\delta=\varepsilon/3<1/2$. The unique global buffered deepest mark is $(0,0)$, of raw mass $Q=3+\delta$ and pure-base depth $4$. The two actual critical caps
$$
X+(1+\delta)z\ge-\delta,\qquad -X+4z\ge-\delta
$$
form a group with weights $1/2,1/2$ and proper own coarea one. For any signed $h$, vary the three interval radii on the same complete base to $(1-ht,1-ht/2,1)$. Continue the cap group's common mass by the exact current contact budget and fixed normals. Its first loss is
$$
\ell(h)=
\begin{cases}
(1+\delta)h/2,&h\ge0,\\
(5+4\delta)h/6,&h\le0.
\end{cases}
$$
The normalized improvement numerator $\ell(h)-(Q/M)3h$ is $-h$ for $h\ge0$ and $(\delta-4)h/6$ for $h\le0$. The Jensen gap $\ell(0)-[\ell(1)+\ell(-1)]/2=(2+\delta)/12>0$ shows the exact continued response is nonadditive and not convex.
title: An actual positive-buffer interval cover with a strict response kink
